title: Wizard Builder for Operational Playflows and Safe Guided Remediations
creator: Asha Patel
description: We will build a small, extensible 'Wizard Builder' that converts curated admin scripts and ad-hoc runbook steps into CLI-backed guided remediation wizards. The goal is to reduce toil for first-line support by offering step-by-step, context-aware guidance that includes automated safe defaults, preflight checks, and one-click audit logging. This is a lightweight layer (tooling + schema) on top of existing runbook assets that produces reproducible, auditable, and testable guided flows.
background: Support has matured a large corpus of bash/python repair scripts and Markdown runbooks. Newer 'runbooks-as-tasks' initiatives provide a runtime but lack UX for non-expert operators. Pager incidents in Q4 showed repeated mistakes from manual playbook execution; several incidents included missing prechecks and manual state inspection. We want a semi-automated wizard that enforces safety checks, records inputs, and can optionally execute idempotent repair commands.
success_criteria: Create wizard schema and CLI generator that can wrap at least 12 existing high-frequency runbooks
Reduce manual step mistakes in pilot by 50% (measured by post-incident checklists)
All wizard executions produce structured audit artifacts (runbook_id, steps_executed, outcome, operator)
Mean time to remediation (MTTR) for pilot flows drops by 20% in first month
acceptance_criteria: Generator produces a validated JSON schema and runnable CLI shim for each source runbook
Each generated wizard includes preflight checks and a dry-run flag
Telemetry events emitted for start/step/end, with error classification
Security review signoff for any wizard that runs privileged actions
implementation_notes: Design an input mapping layer that tags commands with metadata: permissions scope, idempotency, required context (cluster, model-id, dataset). Use the existing admin-runbook registry as the canonical source of truth and a small templating engine to produce the CLI wrapper. Where possible reuse the runbook engine for execution; otherwise embed safe guardrails (confirmation prompts, timeouts, circuit breakers).
architecture_decisions: Use existing runbook runtime for execution to avoid duplicating logic
Wizard metadata is stored as annotated YAML adjacent to runbook artifacts
CLI shim will be implemented in Go (to reuse opsctl tooling) with a thin Python adapter for complex steps
All executions route audit logs to the ops-audit ingest pipeline and a per-wizard dashboard
dependencies: infra/kms-team: key access for privileged step execution
telemetry_goals: Emit event: wizard.start with tags {wizard_id, operator, trigger_source}
Emit event: wizard.step with tags {step_id, status, duration}
Emit event: wizard.end with outcome and error code if any
Surface per-wizard failure rate and avg step latency in console
testing_plan: Unit tests for generator and templating engine
Integration tests that run wizards against a staging cluster with synthetic state
Chaos test: simulate partial step failures and verify rollback/circuit-breaker behavior
User acceptance testing with SRE rotation (3 rotations)
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal alpha for core SREs (3 runbooks)
Phase 1: broaden to Support rotation + collect telemetry (pilot 12 runbooks)
Phase 2: enable self-serve conversion tool in Console for PM-approved runbooks
Rollback: wizard executions can be disabled per-runbook via feature flag
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-automation could hide important context. Mitigation: require explicit context fields and surface raw command preview and dry-run first.
Risk: Privileged steps executed incorrectly. Mitigation: integrate KMS key gating, approval step and RBAC checks.
Risk: Operators become dependent on wizards and lose ad-hoc judgment. Mitigation: training rotations and mandatory docs link in each wizard
